articles.title: Letter: Support the Basketball Court
body: To the editor: I have lived on Oak Avenue for 29 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. has made. Please keep the basketball court in the budget. Many of us on Oak Avenue use it every week.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting.
Gloria Radke, Foundry Row

articles.title: Talia McIver, 77, Carpenter
articles.deck: Friends remember Talia McIver for the many years of service to Foxglove Heights.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foxglove Heights.
Talia McIver died in June at home on Dayton Street, at the age of 77. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Canal Park Food Pantry in his or her name.
Born in Foxglove Heights in the years after the war, Talia McIver spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
